refusalClasses._doc: Q939178BC: the refusal vocabulary collapses to this small, closed set. tools/make-door-contract.py computes each door's own `refusals` (which of these it can return) mechanically from its auth/owner/write fields, and refuses any declared error `class` outside this set — a caller handles three shapes, never fifty-eight.

not-authenticated.meaning: No valid credential reached this door — no session cookie, and no valid Authorization: Bearer token resolved to a person (a key in the address signs no one in).
not-authenticated.nextAction: Authenticate — sign in, send a valid bearer token, or a valid reader key — then retry the exact same call.

not-allowed.meaning: The caller authenticated fine, but its role, scope, or ownership may not do this specific thing (an owner-only door, a read-only OAuth grant on a write tool, a credential that doesn't own the resource).
not-allowed.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged — this is a role/scope/ownership gate, not a transient failure. Use a credential that holds the right role or scope, or ask its holder.

not-found.meaning: The door authenticated the caller fine, but the id/ref/key asked for does not exist, or isn't visible to this caller.
not-found.nextAction: Check the id/ref for a typo or staleness; do not retry the exact same call unchanged.

signIn._doc: THE sign-in rule (D1b, 2026-10-02): ONE rule answers a caller no credential resolved for, on every door, decided in ONE place (src/util.js isBrowserNavigation and signInOr401). Before it, 25 gated pages sent a script with no key to the sign-in page (302) while their checks expected 401.
signIn.browserNavigation: Sec-Fetch-Dest document, or Sec-Fetch-Mode navigate, or (from a client that sends neither) an Accept whose FIRST type is text/html — AND no Authorization header
signIn.navigation: 302 to /login?next=<the path and query asked for, never ?k=> (a form POST: next is the page the form lives on)
signIn.otherwise: 401 JSON {error, hint} — a request that asks for JSON, carries a bearer header (a bad key is a key: 401, never a page), or is a script or a fetch
signIn.idDoors: a door that takes an id answers who is asking BEFORE it looks the id up: signed out, a real id and a made-up one get the same answer; signed in, an id the caller may not read answers not_found exactly as a missing one
signIn.mcp: POST /mcp is a JSON-RPC door: no credential is a JSON-RPC error, never a page

orgArgument._doc: sprint 7, 7.5a (docs/plan/PLATFORM.md §2 items 8 and 9: one /mcp; the OAuth grant carries the person and the org; whoami lists the orgs and a call switches between them). STATELESS: nothing is stored on a grant; each call names its org.
orgArgument.argument: orgSlug: an optional string on EVERY tool (src/index.js ORG_ARG), and ?orgSlug= in a brain:// resource's uri — an org's path name as whoami's orgs lists it; left out, the credential's current org
orgArgument.grants: an OAuth sign-in proved by the ACCOUNT's passphrase makes an ACCOUNT grant (props {personId, accountId, org, scope, cred}: the chosen seat, the account, that seat's org as the grant's current org, the account passphrase's stamp); one proved by a seat's OWN secret makes a SEAT grant (props {personId, scope, cred}: that seat alone — the shape of every grant made before 7.5a, so a client connected before it acts as its seat, unchanged). src/oauthgrants.js
orgArgument.reach: an ACCOUNT grant acts, per call, as the account's own ACTIVE seat in the org named, with that seat's role (never more than the account's seats); a SEAT grant, a bearer key, a session or a read-only credential acts as its one seat: it may name only that seat's org
orgArgument.refusal: org_unreachable — any other org (a seat's credential naming another org; an account grant naming an org it holds no active seat in, or one org per JSON-RPC batch): refused before anything is read or written, the same answer whether the org exists or not, listing only the orgs this credential reaches
orgArgument.ends: an ACCOUNT grant ends when the account's passphrase changes (its stamp); a SEAT grant when that seat's key or passphrase changes (its stamp); a grant carrying NO stamp (made before G2) is refused outright, 401 invalid_token with the re-connect words (7.5b); either when the seat that keys it in the grant store is rotated, re-passworded or removed (src/oauthgrants.js revokeOAuthGrants)
orgArgument.whoami: orgs: [{slug, name, role, current}] (an account grant: every org its account holds an active seat in; any other credential: its one org) and orgNote (how a call picks one)

errors._doc: Q5EB6ACE0: every error code the engine can return, with what it means and what the caller should do next — because the door's primary caller (an MCP-only agent, Q85D42F3F/Q60CCC574) cannot read engine/src to find out. `class` (when present) is one of refusalClasses above; `files`/`live`/`counts.errors` are DERIVED by tools/make-door-contract.py from a live scan of engine/src — this generator FAILS if a live code has no entry here, or a `class` names anything outside refusalClasses. Hand-authored prose, not a generator's guess (no code can state its own meaning).

already_current.meaning: POST /versions/restore (restore_version) named the current version and nothing was filed since it, so there is nothing to restore; or POST /broadcast/equip named the version a project is already on (its newest equip of that slug). Nothing was filed.
already_current.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged: pick an older version from GET /versions (the versions tool) to restore, or another version of the item (GET /broadcast lists the shelf and where this project stands) to equip.

already_decided.meaning: This contribution already carries a terminal decision (approve/reject/needs-work) — decide_contribution and POST /contribution/:id/decide close on the first decide and refuse a second (closed-loop idempotency guard, ADR-072).
already_decided.nextAction: Do not retry — read the row back (read / GET /contribution/:id) to see the decision that already landed.

already_published.meaning: POST /broadcast/publish named a draft that is published already (each draft is one version). Nothing was filed.
already_published.nextAction: Do not retry: file a new draft of the same slug for its next version, then publish that one.

auth_required.meaning: No reader resolved from this request — no session cookie, and no valid Authorization: Bearer token (a key in the address signs no one in).
auth_required.nextAction: Authenticate and retry the exact same call.

bad_consent.meaning: The consent grade sent to /profile isn't one of the allowed values (see the accompanying `allowed` list).
bad_consent.nextAction: Retry with one of the allowed grades.

bad_cursor.meaning: POST /backup-dump?page=<cursor> was sent a cursor no page answered (the dump's pages are walked from "" by each answer's next). Nothing was read.
bad_cursor.nextAction: Start again with page= (empty), and send each answer's next as the following page; next null ends the dump.

bad_field.meaning: A knowledge item sent a field whose value breaks its kind's rule: the wrong type, a value outside its list, a measure, template or options list in the wrong shape, a required field sent empty, a goal naming itself as parent, a node status its type does not take. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops). Or (sprint 3, B1) a contribution's shape field broke its rule (preview, POST /preview): `field` names it (next.by, source[3].kind, depends[0]), with a `hint` and an `example`; nothing was filed.
bad_field.nextAction: Send the field as the error's note says, then the whole batch again.

bad_id.meaning: A knowledge item's key field is missing or malformed (a goal id is a lowercase slug, a qid matches the engine's QID rule, other ids carry no spaces, comma or |, an edge kind is one of the listed ones). Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
bad_id.nextAction: Send the key as the note says, then the whole batch again.

bad_lane.meaning: The lane named isn't one of the org's TX_LANES (see `allowed`).
bad_lane.nextAction: Retry with one of the allowed lanes.

bad_op.meaning: A knowledge item is not {kind, op: "upsert" | "remove", data: {…}}. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
bad_op.nextAction: Send each op in that shape, then the whole batch again.

bad_project.meaning: create_project was sent a key that is not 2 to 40 characters of a-z, 0-9 and dashes, or no name: nothing was created (the same rule POST /control add-project holds).
bad_project.nextAction: Send key as a lowercase slug (e.g. "acme-web") and a name, then create_project again.

bad_ref.meaning: GET /map/node (map {ref}, brain://map/node/{ref}) was sent neither a ref of a known form (screen:<id> · api:<id> · table:<name> · entity:<id> · gap:<id> · goal/<id>) nor a positive integer gap. Nothing was read. Or `read` (GET /read) was sent a ref of no known form (goal/<id> · q/<qid> or question/<qid> · check/<id> · card/<kind>/<id> · doc/<path> · a node id · T-YYYYMMDD-NNN).
bad_ref.nextAction: Retry with a ref of one of those forms, or gap=1 to start the walk over the open gaps.

bad_src.meaning: GET /view's ?src= must be a same-origin path starting with an allowed prefix (see `note`) — refused before proxying anywhere (no open redirect).
bad_src.nextAction: Retry with src set to one of the allowed prefixes.

bad_verdict.meaning: The verdict sent isn't one of the allowed values for this door (decide_contribution: approve/reject/needs-work; submit_grade: proven/refused/incomplete — see `allowed`).
bad_verdict.nextAction: Retry with one of the allowed verdicts.

unsupported_image.meaning: A stored image render's body is not a png, jpeg or webp (an SVG filed before SVG renders were refused): GET /render/:hash answers 410 and does not serve it.
unsupported_image.nextAction: File the render again as a wireframe, or as a png, jpeg or webp picture.

blob_missing.meaning: The artifact's own database row exists, but the R2 object it points at is gone — a storage-layer inconsistency, not a caller mistake.
blob_missing.nextAction: Do not retry the same call — this needs an operator to check storage; report it.

check_id_required.meaning: submit_grade's call needs a `checkId` and none was sent.

client_ref_taken.meaning: This clientRef already filed DIFFERENT content (`filed` names that filing), on any door that takes one: a contribution, a grade, an answer, a wrap-up's card answer or a knowledge write (G2: a clientRef names its content; the same content again is a replay). Nothing was written.
client_ref_taken.nextAction: Send a new clientRef (or leave it out) to file it as new; send the same content to replay it.

content_required.meaning: save_file was sent no content. Nothing was saved.
content_required.nextAction: Retry with content (the document's text or its HTML) and a title.

cross_origin_session_write.meaning: A session-cookie write was attempted from a request this door's CSRF check flags as cross-origin.
cross_origin_session_write.nextAction: Retry from the same origin, or use a bearer token instead of a cookie session for a script/cross-origin caller.

cross_site_login.meaning: POST /login was flagged as arriving from a different site than this door (Sec-Fetch-Site, or Origin when that header is absent) — the login-CSRF guard (heal round 1, QC74D4892 verifier finding: an org's own /login used to have none).
cross_site_login.nextAction: Sign in from the door's own page (this is refused before any credential is even read) — a script/CLI client (curl, the suites) sends neither header and is never flagged.

d1_quota.meaning: Cloudflare D1's daily free-tier row-read budget is exhausted for this worker — every authenticated call fails until it resets at 00:00 UTC (see `retryAfterMinutes`). Nothing is lost; this is an infrastructure ceiling, not anything about the call itself.
d1_quota.nextAction: Wait until the reset time in `retryAfterMinutes`, then retry — retrying sooner will not succeed, and no input change fixes it.

empty.meaning: The content/body sent (e.g. to save_file) was empty — zero bytes.

forbidden.meaning: The caller authenticated, but may not read/write this specific resource (a role's brief it can't read, a private artifact it doesn't own). Or, inside a preview then save_knowledge invalid_ops, a non-owner's op on a doc, a card or a card kind their role may not read, or on a card of such a kind.
forbidden.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged — use a credential that holds the resource, or ask its owner.

goal_cycle.meaning: A knowledge batch would make a goal its own ancestor. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
goal_cycle.nextAction: Point the goal's parent at a goal outside its own branch, then send the batch again.

goal_roots.meaning: A knowledge batch would leave the project's goal tree with more than one root (a goal with no parent), or none. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
goal_roots.nextAction: Give every goal but the one root a parent, then send the batch again.

group_required.meaning: save_file needs a real `group` (which system-part this belongs to) — 'ungrouped' is refused outright by the schema.
group_required.nextAction: Retry with a real group name.

has_children.meaning: A knowledge remove names a goal that still has child goals the batch does not remove. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
has_children.nextAction: Remove the children in the same batch, or give them another parent first.

id_required.meaning: The call needs an `id` (or, for the pack door, `kind`+`id`) and none was sent.

incomplete_item.meaning: POST /broadcast/publish named a draft that is not complete (its grade is incomplete: what, why, touches naming one of skill, agent or workflow, gapRefs ["item/<slug>"] and a source link as proof). Nothing was filed.
incomplete_item.nextAction: File the draft again with every field (FILING_ITEM_CALL), then publish the new one.

insufficient_scope.meaning: This MCP connection was granted read-only access (mcp:read); the tool called needs mcp:write.
insufficient_scope.nextAction: Reconnect with mcp:write, or ask whoever granted the connection to widen its scope — do not retry unchanged.

invalid_login.meaning: The email/password pair sent to POST /login didn't match a live account.
invalid_login.nextAction: Retry with the correct credentials — this is not a transient failure.

no_seat_here.meaning: POST /login: the email and password are right, but that account holds no seat in the org this address serves (sprint 7: one account per email, a seat per org). Nothing was signed in, and never a seat of another org. Also (sprint 7's review, A1) when your account's only seats WAIT for your yes (an org's admin added you while your account stood elsewhere): a JSON sign-in mints nothing until you accept them on your org list.
no_seat_here.nextAction: Ask this org's admin to add you, or sign in at the address of the org your seat is in.

invalid_ops.meaning: At least one knowledge item broke a rule, so NOTHING in the batch was written; `errors` lists each one as { index, kind, id, error, note } (the first 100; `count` is all of them).
invalid_ops.nextAction: Fix every op named, then send the whole batch again (the same clientRef is fine: nothing was filed under it).

items_required.meaning: A preview's or a write tool's body carried no items array (or an empty one, or over 200 for a write tool).
items_required.nextAction: Retry with at least one item.

kind_and_id_required.meaning: The pack door call needs both `kind` and `id`, and at least one was missing.

missing_field.meaning: A knowledge upsert creates a new item without one of its kind's required fields (a goal's title, a question's question, a check's title, a card's name, a node's type and name, a doc's body, the aim, the template). Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
missing_field.nextAction: Send the field the note names, then the whole batch again.

missing_card.meaning: A knowledge card names in its refs a card that this project does not hold, or one the writer may not read, at the end of the batch (sprint 4, F1). Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops); the note and `near` name up to three of the project's own cards close to each missed ref.
missing_card.nextAction: Send refs as cards of this project, card/<kind>/<id> (read kind card lists them), or file that card in the same batch.

unknown_project.meaning: A knowledge node names in ownedBy (its data.ownedBy, or a part of its architecture's diagram) a project key that is not an active project the writer may read (sprint 4, M3: a name check on the org's projects, the writer's seats or, for the owner, every active project). Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops); `projects` lists the keys the writer may name, never the project written.
unknown_project.nextAction: Send ownedBy as one of `projects`, or leave it out.

missing_node.meaning: A knowledge edge names a node that is not in the project at the end of the batch, or a render names a screen that is not a node of type screen there. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
missing_node.nextAction: File the node first (kind node; a render's screen as type screen), in the same batch or before.

missing_parent.meaning: A knowledge goal names a parent that is not a goal of the project at the end of the batch. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
missing_parent.nextAction: Send an existing goal's id as parent (read kind goal lists them), or file that parent in the same batch.

no_choice.meaning: A knowledge question is ruled (not open) and has options, yet names no choice (an option index or letter) and carries no label. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
no_choice.nextAction: Send choice as the option's index (0 = A) or letter, or a label saying what was ruled.

no_session.meaning: There is no session token on this request to act on (nothing to sign out, or nothing changed).
no_session.nextAction: Nothing to retry — this caller was already signed out or had nothing to change.

not_filed.meaning: The round filing did not reach the ledger and returned no reason of its own (a store hiccup, not the caller's input).
not_filed.nextAction: Retry once; if it repeats, report it with the time.

not_found.meaning: The door authenticated the caller fine, but the id/ref/key asked for does not exist, or isn't visible to this caller.
not_found.nextAction: Check the id for a typo; do not retry the same call unchanged.

not_open.meaning: The question is already ruled (decided, provisional, superseded or moot), so it takes no answer. Nothing was filed.
not_open.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged: read the ruling with `decisions` and its qid; to argue with it, file a counter as the card's counterCall says.

not_seated.meaning: POST /broadcast/equip named a project the caller holds no seat on (the owner may equip into any active project), or POST /broadcast/publish was pressed by a person seated nowhere in the org. Nothing was filed.
not_seated.nextAction: Equip into a project you are seated on, or ask a person seated on that project (or the owner) to press it.

not_yours.meaning: POST /broadcast/publish named a draft (kind item) that another person filed. Only a draft's own author publishes it. Nothing was filed. POST /orgs/seat (sprint 7's review, A1): the seat named is not one of YOUR account's seats waiting for your yes (another account's, one no longer waiting, or the request is not your own ACCOUNT session): HTTP 404, nothing changed, the same answer for every case.
not_yours.nextAction: Publish one of your own drafts (GET /broadcast lists them under mine), or file your own with FILING_ITEM_CALL. For a seat: answer it from your org list (GET /orgs), signed in with your account's passphrase.

only_owner.meaning: POST /orgs/seat with answer decline (2026-10-15, THE FIRST PASSPHRASE WAITS): the waiting seat is its org's only real owner, so declining it would leave the org with no active owner. HTTP 409, nothing changed: the seat still waits.
only_owner.nextAction: Accept the seat from your org list (GET /orgs), or leave it waiting.

open_has_choice.meaning: A knowledge question is open yet carries a choice. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
open_has_choice.nextAction: Send choice null, or (the owner) rule it with status decided.

ops_required.meaning: The knowledge write behind file carried no items, or an empty list. Nothing was written.
ops_required.nextAction: Send ops: a list of 1 to 200 {kind, op, data}.

option_required.meaning: An answer to a published question is one of its options, chosen, never typed text (QBDD22130): the call carried free text (answer, a legacy item, an a_*/x_* field) or no integer option. Nothing was filed.
option_required.nextAction: Retry with qid and option, the index of one of the question's published options (0 for A, 1 for B, 2 for C); `decisions` lists them.

owner_only.meaning: This door/tool is owner-role only, and the caller isn't the org's owner. Or, inside a preview then save_knowledge invalid_ops, a member's op on a question's ruling: a status other than open, a choice, label, rationale, decidedBy, decidedAt or supersededBy, or an edit or remove of a ruled question; a non-owner writing a role's brief doc capsules/<role>.md or start-here.md; or a non-owner setting or changing roleVisibility.
owner_only.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged — use the owner's own credential, or ask the owner to do this.

project_forbidden.meaning: The `project` named isn't one the caller may use: not one of their own seats (the owner: not an ACTIVE project) — on a write, or (U-MCP, projectScope) on a project-scoped READ at any door: an MCP tool's `project`, a GET twin's ?project= (403) or a brain:// resource's ?project= (-32003); or (U-MCP-tail-b) a non-string `project` (an object, array, number or boolean — `project` is one project key, a string); or an answer naming another project than its call (respond / round: one project per answer call). Nothing was read or filed. `seats` lists the allowed projects. Or (the knowledge door) a write to a project the caller holds no seat on, even the one project of a single-project org the door would otherwise stamp them into.
project_forbidden.nextAction: Retry with one of the seats listed (the refusal's `note` and `example` name them), or ask for a seat on the project named.

project_required.meaning: This caller holds more than one seat, so the write needs an explicit `project` to stamp — the server refuses to guess; or POST /broadcast/equip named no project and the request has none of its own; or (U-MCP-tail-b D6) submit_grade has no project to count against (a caller seated nowhere in a multi-project org) or its filing would be stamped into another project than the pack it reads — nothing is filed. Or preview / read resolved no project (a caller holding more than one seat with none active, or the owner seated nowhere in a multi-project org): nothing is written or read.
project_required.nextAction: Retry with `project` set to one of the seats listed — the refusal's `note` names them and its `example` carries one ready to send (for an equip: the project to equip into).

q_required.meaning: search (or GET /search) carried no search words (`q`; search counts words of two letters and up). Nothing was read.

question_required.meaning: The `ask` call carried no `question` — nothing to ask.
question_required.nextAction: Retry with `question`: what you want to ask the owner.

read_only_credential.meaning: The credential used (e.g. a boot link / read-only key) can read but not write.
read_only_credential.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged — use the full write-capable credential.

ref_required.meaning: The call needs a canonical `ref` (screen:NNN · c/<id> · q/<id> · mind/<area>) and none was sent; `read` (GET /read) was sent neither a ref nor a kind; or regrade (POST /regrade) was sent none of flow, node or checks.
ref_required.nextAction: Retry with `ref` (regrade: flow, node or checks).

ref_too_long.meaning: The `ref` sent is over the 80-character limit (see `max`).

reserved_kind.meaning: A filing with kind publish, equip or knowledge reached file_contribution (a contribution item). Publish and equip are written only by a person's press on Broadcast, knowledge only by the knowledge write door (one row per save_knowledge or remove_knowledge call). Nothing was filed (a batch files none of its items).
reserved_kind.nextAction: Do not retry with that kind: file a draft as kind item (FILING_ITEM_CALL) and let its author press Publish, or the people seated on a project press Equip, on Broadcast; write knowledge with preview then save_knowledge (POST /preview/save-knowledge).

slug_required.meaning: equip (or POST /broadcast/equip) was sent no slug: the item to equip, a slug on the shelf or preset:<slug> for a starter item. Nothing was read or filed.
slug_required.nextAction: Retry with slug and v: `broadcast` lists the shelf and the starter items, each with its slug and version.

slug_taken.meaning: POST /broadcast/publish named a draft whose item/<slug> another person published first; a slug belongs to its first publisher. Nothing was filed.
slug_taken.nextAction: File the draft again under another slug, then publish that one.

plan_limit.meaning: The org is at a limit of its plan (sprint 8, docs/plan/PLATFORM.md §4: the ruled free and team numbers), and this WRITE would take it past: `limit` names which (people: seats active or waiting for their holder's yes; projects: active projects; items_month: ledger rows filed this UTC month — contributions, knowledge writes, grades; calls_day: MCP tools/calls and REST writes this UTC day; burst_minute: the same calls this minute; storage_bytes: stored files and screen pictures, each body once — src/plans.js STORAGE_USED_SQL, the one definition the check and the shown plan read; checked by a file upload and, since 8.5, by a knowledge write's new render or style bodies before any is stored), `used` and `allowed` the org's own numbers, `plan` the plan whose limits applied (an org whose plan names none reads free's), `adding` what a batch or a file would add, `retryAfter` the seconds until a calls window starts again. Nothing was written. Reads are never refused. A call refused at the door is HTTP 429 with Retry-After; a write past 80% of a limit lands and its answer carries planWarning {limit, used, allowed, plan, note} (a REST write also the x-sharingu-plan-warning header).
plan_limit.nextAction: For burst_minute or calls_day: wait retryAfter seconds, then send the same call. For any other limit: do not retry unchanged — free room (archive a project, remove a seat or a file) or ask the operator, who raises an org's limits by hand during the beta.

org_suspended.meaning: The operator has suspended this org (sprint 8, 8.5: tools/operator.mjs suspend; the one key `suspended` in its org row's settings). Every door answers the org's own people this one 403 — its pages, its MCP calls, its REST calls and a sign-in's landing in it — and nothing is routed, counted or written. Nothing of the org was deleted: when the operator lifts the suspension (unsuspend) every read and write answers as before. It takes hold within a minute (the org row is cached a minute per isolate); lifting it is answered at once (a suspended row is read fresh before each 403). Anyone else meets what they always met (another org's credential: the one not-here answer).
org_suspended.nextAction: Do not retry: ask the operator, who suspends and lifts an org by hand during the beta.

summary_required.meaning: wrap_up needs a `summary` and none was sent.

title_required.meaning: The call needs a `title` and none was sent.

too_few_options.meaning: A knowledge question would end the batch open with fewer than 2 options, or ruled with exactly one. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
too_few_options.nextAction: Send data.options with 2 or more [{what, tradeoff}] (a ruling may carry none).

too_large.meaning: The content sent is over this door's byte limit (see `maxBytes`); on preview then save_knowledge (inside invalid_ops), a render's or a style's body over its limit (html 200 KB, css 200 KB, a wireframe 50 KB, an image 1 MB), a call whose carried bodies (html, css, wireframes) together pass 256 KB, or whose image renders' pictures together pass 1 MB — the error's index names the op.
too_large.nextAction: Retry with smaller content, or split it (a call's bodies: send the named op and the ones after it in another call).

too_many_attempts.meaning: This account has failed sign-in too many times; a per-account cooldown is active (see `retryAfterMinutes`).
too_many_attempts.nextAction: Wait the stated cooldown before retrying — retrying sooner will not succeed.

too_many_attempts_ip.meaning: This IP has failed sign-in too many times; a per-IP cooldown is active (see `retryAfterSeconds`).
too_many_attempts_ip.nextAction: Wait the stated cooldown before retrying.

too_many_items.meaning: A preview carried more than 200 items, or regrade (POST /regrade) named more than 60 checks (see `max`/`got`).
too_many_items.nextAction: Split into previews of 200 or fewer, or regrades of 60 checks or fewer.

too_many_ops.meaning: A preview or file carried more than 200 items (see `max`/`got`). Nothing was written.
too_many_ops.nextAction: Split the batch into calls of 200 ops or fewer.

transcript_rejected.meaning: The privacy door (ADR-016 d) refused this call because it appears to carry a raw conversation transcript.
transcript_rejected.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged — strip the transcript content and resend just the real payload.

unauthorized.meaning: The bearer token sent didn't resolve to a person (missing, malformed, expired, or revoked).
unauthorized.nextAction: Send a valid Authorization: Bearer <token> and retry.

unimplemented.meaning: The tool name called isn't wired to a handler in callTool's switch — a registry/implementation mismatch, not a caller mistake.
unimplemented.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged — report it; this is an engine defect.

unknown_field.meaning: A knowledge upsert sent a field its kind does not have. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
unknown_field.nextAction: Send only the fields the note lists (formats {kind} lists every kind's), then the whole batch again.

unknown_goal.meaning: GET /goals/:ref (the goal tool, brain://goal/{ref}) named a goal id that is not in this workspace's goal tree: missing, mistyped, or another project's (the same answer either way, M-ADR-028). Nothing was read.
unknown_goal.nextAction: Read GET /goals (the goals tool) and use one of its nodes[].id; do not retry the same ref unchanged.

unknown_item.meaning: POST /broadcast/publish named no filing of kind item by that id, or POST /broadcast/equip named a slug nothing on the shelf carries. Nothing was filed.
unknown_item.nextAction: Read GET /broadcast (the broadcast tool): mine lists your drafts' ids, the shelf the published slugs.

unknown_kind.meaning: The kind named isn't one the door knows: a knowledge item, a read / GET /read kind or a formats / GET /formats kind outside aim · goal · question · check · card · card_kind · node · edge · gtm · doc · render · style (see `kinds`), or a pack kind this workspace's pack does not declare. For search, read and changes: a kind outside the list their answer names in `kinds`.
unknown_kind.nextAction: Retry with one of the kinds listed.

unknown_node.meaning: GET /map/node (map {ref}, brain://map/node/{ref}) named a node the published map does not carry: an unknown screen, door, table, entity or gap, a goal not in the served goal tree, or a gap index past the last OPEN gap; or regrade (POST /regrade) named a flow or a node the project does not hold. Nothing was regraded.
unknown_node.nextAction: Read GET /map/node?gap=1 (walk.n is the open-gap count) or GET /canvas.json for the ids the map carries; do not retry the same ref unchanged.

path_required.meaning: doc (GET /doc/:path) was called without a path. Nothing was read.
path_required.nextAction: Send path: one of the docs `read` lists; start-here.md is the place to start.

unknown_check.meaning: submit_grade (POST /grade) or regrade (POST /regrade, checks) named a checkId the project's check register (k_checks) does not carry. Nothing was filed or regraded.
unknown_check.nextAction: List the project's checks with read {kind: "check"} (brief {for: <a ref>} for one item's), then retry with one of their ids; file a new check as an item {kind: "check", op: "upsert", data} through preview, then save_knowledge.

unknown_option.meaning: The option index is not one of the question's published options. Nothing was filed.
unknown_option.nextAction: Read the question (`decisions` with its qid, or GET /question/:qid) and retry with one of its option indexes.

unknown_parent.meaning: The `parent` named is not a filing in the caller's project: no such id, or a filing in a project the caller holds no seat on (the two read the same, so the refusal never says a row exists elsewhere). Nothing was filed; a batch naming one is refused whole.
unknown_parent.nextAction: Name an existing filing of your project as parent (read / GET /build list what you can see), or counter a question with gapRefs ["q/<qid>"] instead; then retry.

unknown_plane.meaning: GET /map/:plane (map {plane}, brain://map/{plane}) named a plane this worker does not serve: the served planes are arch, data, api, mcp, flows and deps (System is GET /map itself).
unknown_plane.nextAction: Read one of the planes the answer lists (planes), or GET /map for System; do not retry the same plane unchanged.

unknown_qid.meaning: No published question carries this qid (or nothing is published for this project). Nothing was filed.
unknown_qid.nextAction: Check the qid against `decisions` (GET /decisions); do not retry the same call unchanged.

unknown_table.meaning: GET /map/data?table=<name> (map {plane} {plane:'data', table}) named a table the project's model (D1) does not carry. The answer lists the tables it does.
unknown_table.nextAction: Pick one of the listed tables (tables); do not retry the same name unchanged.

unknown_version.meaning: GET /versions/:v, POST /versions/restore or the versions tools named a version (a number or a content key) this project's spine does not carry; or POST /broadcast/equip named a version of an item beyond its newest (v1 to vN, the n-th publish). Nothing was filed. Or `changes` (GET /changes) was sent since: v<N> for a version the project does not carry. Nothing was read.
unknown_version.nextAction: Read GET /versions (the versions tool) for the versions that exist, or GET /broadcast for an item's newest version, then retry with one of them.

unreadable.meaning: The served state itself is marked unreadable, or (UI-B2: GET /decisions, GET /question/:qid) the published pack names a decisions file that is missing or not a list — a data problem on sharingu's own side, not the caller's; or (UI-B7b: GET /map/node; UI-B8b: GET /map/:plane arch and data, map {plane}) the canvas asset could not be read from storage.
unreadable.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged — report it; this needs the brain's own state (or its pack publish) checked.

write_failed.meaning: The knowledge batch passed every rule but the database refused it (the message rides in the note); D1 applies the batch and its ledger row together, so in the usual case nothing was written.
write_failed.nextAction: Read the kinds back before retrying; a retry with the same clientRef is safe (a write that did land answers replay).

partner_refused.meaning: publish, equip or regrade (the MCP tools, or their REST twins POST /broadcast/publish, POST /broadcast/equip and POST /regrade), or a restore of a screen's take (a render upsert naming a take's hash on preview then save_knowledge, inside invalid_ops; POST /render/restore), was called by a Partner: the role CLASS (src/hats.js roleClassOf: people.role partner, or a typed outside label such as external-* or vendor). An outside collaborator works on the projects they are seated on and never publishes to the org's shelf, equips into a project, regrades its checks or restores a screen's previous take. Nothing was read or filed.
partner_refused.nextAction: Ask a member of the org to publish the draft, equip the item or regrade the checks or restore the take, or ask the admin to make you a member on Control.

bad_hat.meaning: POST /profile set-profile named a hat that is not one of the seven (management · engineering · organization · gtm · finance · partner · quality). Nothing was saved.
bad_hat.nextAction: Retry with hats from the accompanying `allowed` list (an empty list clears your hats).

missing_artifact.meaning: A knowledge image render names an artifact that does not exist or that you may not use (not one you banked, not public; the owner may use any). The two read the same, so an id is never confirmed to someone who cannot read it. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
missing_artifact.nextAction: Bank the picture yourself (save_file, or POST /artifact with its image content type: png, jpeg or webp; an SVG is refused, file a wireframe instead) and send that id as data.artifact. The artifact must be your own or a public one.

missing_style.meaning: A knowledge render names a style that is not in the project at the end of the batch. Nothing was written (it rides in invalid_ops).
missing_style.nextAction: File the style first (kind style, {id, css}), in the same batch or before, or leave style out.

unknown_surface.meaning: GET /map/screens (map {plane: "screens"}) named a surface the project's screens do not name. Nothing else was read.
unknown_surface.nextAction: Send one of the surfaces the answer lists (a screen node names its surface in data.surface), or leave surface out for the first.

unknown_shape.meaning: formats (or GET /formats) named a shape that is not a lane. The answer lists the shapes.
unknown_shape.nextAction: Send shape as one of the listed lanes.

preview_id_required.meaning: file was sent no previewId of the form preview answers (P- and 16 hex). Nothing was filed.
preview_id_required.nextAction: Send previewId: the id preview answered, and the items of the tool's operation, as previewed.

preview_not_found.meaning: A write tool (file_contribution, save_knowledge, remove_knowledge) named a preview that is not the caller's own: none with that id, or another person's (the same answer either way, so an id grants nothing). GET /preview/:id answers its usual 404 for the same reasons. Nothing was filed.
preview_not_found.nextAction: Preview the items again (preview) and file with the id it answers.

preview_filed.meaning: A write tool named a preview whose part of that operation was already filed; nothing was filed again. The answer carries that part's first receipt (what each item became).
preview_filed.nextAction: Nothing: read the receipt. File the preview's other parts with their own tools, or preview again to file something new.

preview_expired.meaning: A write tool named a preview older than an hour, and nothing of its part had been filed. Nothing was filed.
preview_expired.nextAction: Preview the items again, then file with the new previewId.

preview_changed.meaning: A write tool was sent items whose digest (sha256 of the items as canonical JSON) differs from the preview's items of its operation, in their order: what would be filed is not what the person saw (or the preview was made before the split, sprint 19). Nothing was filed; items names the preview's items of that operation.
preview_changed.nextAction: Send the preview's items of that operation as previewed, or preview again, then file with the new previewId.

not_ready.meaning: A write tool named a preview whose items of its operation are not all ready (verdict needs or refused), and the call did not ask for only "ready". Nothing was filed; notReady lists each such item's index and verdict.
not_ready.nextAction: Fix those items and preview again, or call the tool again with only: "ready" to file the ready ones and leave the rest.

wrong_tool.meaning: sprint 19 (the split door): a write tool was sent an item of another operation (items names each, what it is and the tool that files it: file_contribution a contribution, save_knowledge a knowledge upsert, remove_knowledge a knowledge remove; submit_grade a grade, respond an answer), or preview was sent a grade or an answer (that item is refused, naming submit_grade or respond). Nothing was filed.
wrong_tool.nextAction: Send each write tool only the preview's items of its own operation, as previewed; file a grade with submit_grade and an answer with respond.

nothing_to_file.meaning: sprint 19: a write tool named a preview that holds no item of its operation (parts names each tool the preview's items are filed with). Nothing was filed.
nothing_to_file.nextAction: Call the tool the parts name, with its items.

batch_failed.meaning: One grade or answer of a call did not come back from the batch door, so it is not filed; the answer names it, the others stand.
batch_failed.nextAction: Send the same call again with the same clientRefs: what landed is found by its clientRef and never filed twice.

unreachable.meaning: GET /preview/:id (JSON) could not read the preview right now (a D1 error other than the daily limit). Nothing was read or written.

no_next_action.meaning: pick_up was sent a contribution that names no next action (its next {what, who?, by?}), so there is nothing to take. Nothing changed.
no_next_action.nextAction: Read the contribution; a next action is filed with it (next {what, who?, by?}), or file a new contribution with one.

next_taken.meaning: Someone else picked up this contribution's next action first; the answer's pickedUp names who and when. The first pick-up holds. Nothing changed.
next_taken.nextAction: Do not retry unchanged: ask the person who holds it, or wait until they mark it done or release it. The contribution itself stays open to anyone.

next_done.meaning: This contribution's next action is done already (the answer's done says when and by whom: a person's pick_up done, or a later contribution naming it as parent). Nothing changed.
next_done.nextAction: Do not retry: file a new contribution with its own next action if more is owed.

not_picked_up.meaning: pick_up release was sent for a next action nobody holds. Nothing changed.
not_picked_up.nextAction: Nothing to release; pick it up instead if it is yours to take.

release_forbidden.meaning: Only the person holding a next action, the contribution's contributor or the owner releases it. Nothing changed.
release_forbidden.nextAction: Ask the person holding it (the answer's pickedUp names them) or the owner.

refs_required.meaning: impact was sent neither a contribution id nor any ref it can read. Nothing was read.
refs_required.nextAction: Send contribution: an id (T-YYYYMMDD-NNN), or refs: the ids you are about to change (screen:<id>, door:<method>:<path>, goal/<id>, q/<qid>, check/<id>).

search_unavailable.meaning: search (GET /search) found no full-text index on this org: migrate-056 is not applied yet. Nothing was read.
search_unavailable.nextAction: Use `read` with a kind to list items meanwhile; the admin applies migrate-056.

bad_since.meaning: changes (GET /changes) was sent a since that is neither an ISO time nor a version (v4). Nothing was read.
bad_since.nextAction: Retry with since: 2026-10-01, 2026-10-01T09:00:00Z or v4, or leave it out for the current version.

bad_state.meaning: changes {org: true, list: true} (GET /changes?org=1&list=1, GET /audit?all=1) was sent a state outside landed · with · decided · needs. Nothing was read.
bad_state.nextAction: Retry with one of the states listed in `allowed`, or leave it out.

bad_person.meaning: changes {org: true, list: true} was sent a person that is not a person's id. Nothing was read.
bad_person.nextAction: Send an item's by.id (whoami answers your own), or leave person out.

bad_before.meaning: changes {org: true, list: true} was sent a before that is not a cursor this read gave. Nothing was read.
bad_before.nextAction: Send the previous answer's next exactly as it came, or leave before out for the newest page.

unknown_tab.meaning: changes (GET /changes) was sent a tab outside home · build · gtm · goals · decisions · map · broadcast · control. Nothing was read.
unknown_tab.nextAction: Retry with one of the tabs listed in `tabs`, or leave it out.

for_required.meaning: brief (GET /brief) was sent no `for`: a hat or a ref. Nothing was read.
for_required.nextAction: Retry with for: a hat (management, engineering, organization, gtm, finance, partner, quality) or a ref (goal/<id>, q/<qid>, check/<id>, a node id, T-YYYYMMDD-NNN).

bad_answer.meaning: A JSON-RPC response POSTed to /mcp (a client's answer to a confirm, sprint 3 D3) was neither an elicitation result (action accept, decline or cancel) nor a JSON-RPC error. HTTP 400; nothing was recorded or filed.
bad_answer.nextAction: Answer the elicitation/create request with {action, content} as the MCP elicitation spec shapes it, or send the write tool's call again without fileOnConfirm once the person said yes.

confirm_failed.meaning: The confirm's stream (a write tool with fileOnConfirm, sprint 19; publish or equip with its OnConfirm flag, 7.5b) could not finish: a database call failed while it waited or filed. Nothing more was filed by the stream; what landed before is in the preview's receipt.
confirm_failed.nextAction: Send the same call again without fileOnConfirm: a retry files only what did not land.

confirm_not_open.meaning: A client's answer to a confirm named no open confirm of the caller's: another person's elicitation, another session's, a wrong id, an answer after the window (50 s), a second answer, a preview already filed, or (7.5b) a retry naming another tool's confirm (sprint 19: another write tool's too) or a changed call (the same answer for each, so an id grants nothing). HTTP 400; nothing was recorded or filed.
confirm_not_open.nextAction: Nothing to retry: call the write tool again with fileOnConfirm for a new confirm, or without it once the person said yes.

session_required.meaning: A client's answer to a confirm came without the Mcp-Session-Id header the initialize answer gave; a confirm is bound to the session that asked. HTTP 400; nothing recorded.
session_required.nextAction: Send the answer with the session id initialize answered (Mcp-Session-Id).

unknown_response.meaning: A JSON-RPC response POSTed to /mcp answers no request this door sent (the door sends only elicitation/create on a confirm's stream, with an id sg-confirm:<previewId>:<nonce>). HTTP 400; nothing recorded.
unknown_response.nextAction: Do not send responses except to the door's own elicitation/create request.

unknown_brief.meaning: brief with no `for` (or GET /brief?role=) named a role whose brief (the doc capsules/<role>.md) the project does not hold, or one your role may not read: the two read the same (see `briefs`).
unknown_brief.nextAction: Name one of `briefs` as role, or file the brief: preview then save_knowledge, a doc at capsules/<role>.md.

invalid_token.meaning: An OAuth access token the provider still holds, whose person the door refuses: their key or passphrase changed after the grant (G2 M1), or they were removed; or a grant made before connections carried their credentials' stamp (before G2: sprint 7, 7.5b — it could never be checked, so it ends; its error_description says so). Nothing was read or written.
invalid_token.nextAction: Connect the app again (the OAuth sign-in) — do not retry the same token.

no_owner.meaning: The report backfill found no active owner to hold the reports it banks. Nothing was banked.
no_owner.nextAction: Restore an active owner on /control, then run POST /backfill again.

eval_mark_refused.meaning: The eval mark (a test run's own row: hidden from every real screen, removed by Control's clean-eval) was sent on a write to a real project by a person who is not a test seat. Nothing was filed.
eval_mark_refused.nextAction: Leave eval out to file it for real, or file the test on an eval project (create_project {eval: true}) or as a test seat.

unknown_render.meaning: A render upsert that restores a take (data.hash, no body) names a hash this project's takes do not hold: never filed here, or another project's (the two read the same). On preview then save_knowledge it rides in invalid_ops (nothing was written); POST /render/restore answers it 404.
unknown_render.nextAction: Send the hash of one of this project's takes (map {ref: "screen:<id>"} lists a screen's last six, each with its hash), or send the frame's body instead.

invalid_signup.meaning: POST /signup (sprint 7, 7.2): the email and code do not open a sign-up. ONE answer for every case: the email was never allowed by the operator, or the code is wrong, already used, expired, revoked, or was given for another email. Nothing was written but the attempt, which counts in the account's lockout with the sign-in's failures.
invalid_signup.nextAction: Check the email and the code against the email that brought the code (sharingu sends it when a place opens); a lost, used or expired code is replaced only by the operator.

bad_signup.meaning: POST /signup (sprint 7, 7.2): a field is missing or malformed, checked before anything is read (`field`: email · code · passphrase · confirm, with a `note`). It says nothing about which emails are allowed.
bad_signup.nextAction: Fix the named field and send again: an email address, the code as given, a passphrase of at least 4 characters, the same passphrase twice.

invalid_invite.meaning: POST /signup with an org's invite link (sprint 12, 12.3): the link does not open a sign-up. ONE answer for every case: no such open link, already used, expired (7 days), replaced by a newer link for the same seat, or its seat was removed, reissued (a new key or passphrase set by the admin) or is waiting for its holder's yes. Nothing was written, not even an attempt.
invalid_invite.nextAction: Ask the admin who invited you for a new link (Control: the person's row, New invite link).

account_stands.meaning: POST /signup with an org's invite link (sprint 12, 12.3): the invited email's account already stands — it holds its own passphrase, or a seat in another org — so the link sets no passphrase and changed nothing (no passphrase, no seat, the link not spent).
account_stands.nextAction: Sign in at /login with your account passphrase; if the seat waits for your yes, accept it on your org list (GET /orgs). An account with no passphrase yet gets one by the operator's sign-up code (POST /signup).

bad_invite.meaning: POST /signup with an org's invite link (sprint 12, 12.3): a field is missing or malformed, checked before anything is read (`field`: invite · passphrase · confirm, with a `note`): the invite is the link's 48-character token (the whole link is taken too), the passphrase at least 12 characters.
bad_invite.nextAction: Open the invite link again (or paste it whole), and choose a passphrase of at least 12 characters, the same one twice.

org_by_invite.meaning: POST /orgs (sprint 12, 12.3): the account's passphrase was set by an org's invite link, so it proves only what that org's admin could hand over: it creates no org during the beta (the orgs join by the waitlist, the owner approving each). Nothing written but the proof's attempt.
org_by_invite.nextAction: Ask the sharingu operator for a sign-up code: it confirms your email (POST /signup resets the passphrase and lifts the mark), then create your org.

cross_site_signup.meaning: POST /signup was flagged as arriving from a different site than this door (Sec-Fetch-Site, or Origin when that header is absent), the same guard as POST /login's cross_site_login. Refused before the body is read: nothing written, not even an attempt.
cross_site_signup.nextAction: Sign up from the door's own page; a script client sends neither header and is never flagged.

bad_request_access.meaning: POST /request-access (sprint 21, 21.1): a field is missing or malformed, checked before anything is written (`field`: name · email · company · role · team_size · website · linkedin · x · github · ai_tools · use_case, with a `note`): name, a plain-ASCII work email, company, role and a team size of 1, 2-10, 11-50, 51-200 or 201+ are required; website an http(s) address (a bare domain is taken), linkedin, x and github that service's address or a handle. It says nothing about who asked before or holds an account.
bad_request_access.nextAction: Fix the named field and send again; leave an optional field empty rather than guessing.

cross_site_request_access.meaning: POST /request-access was flagged as arriving from a different site than this door (Sec-Fetch-Site, or Origin when that header is absent), the same guard as POST /login's cross_site_login. Refused before the body is read: nothing written.
cross_site_request_access.nextAction: Request access from the door's own page (GET /request-access); a script client sends neither header and is never flagged.

email_unverified.meaning: POST /login (a script) for an email that holds no account yet, with the passphrase of its newest unverified join (sprint 21, 21.4a: the account flow): the email was never verified, so no account exists and nothing is signed in.
email_unverified.nextAction: Open the verification link the join's email carries (POST /account/resend {email} sends a new one), type the passphrase there, then sign in.

invalid_link.meaning: POST /account/verify or POST /account/reset with a link that opens nothing (sprint 21, 21.4a): expired (a verification works 24 hours, a reset 30 minutes), used already, never sent, or (a verification) a verified request of that email stands. ONE answer for every case; nothing written.
invalid_link.nextAction: Ask for a new link: POST /account/resend {email} (a verification) or POST /account/forgot {email} (a reset).

wrong_passphrase.meaning: POST /account/verify with a live link but a passphrase that is not the one the join chose (sprint 21, 21.4a): the mailbox alone does not verify a request, so a stranger's join for an address cannot be completed by its owner's click. The attempt counts in the email's lockout; the request stays unverified.
wrong_passphrase.nextAction: Type the passphrase chosen when asking to join (8 failures in 15 minutes are 429 too_many_attempts).

google_join_expired.meaning: POST /request-access with google=1 (sprint 21, 21.4c: the form Google filled in) when this browser holds no live Google identity for it: the join ticket was used, is past its 30 minutes, or was made in another browser. HTTP 410; nothing written.
google_join_expired.nextAction: Continue with Google again (GET /auth/google/start?intent=join), or join with your email and a passphrase (POST /request-access without google).

account_exists.meaning: POST /request-access with google=1 (sprint 21, 21.4c) for an email an account holds by now (or a Google account another account is linked to): nothing was filed. HTTP 409.
account_exists.nextAction: Sign in instead: Continue with Google (GET /auth/google/start?intent=signin) or POST /login with the account's passphrase.

bad_email.meaning: POST /account/resend or POST /account/forgot whose email is not one plain ASCII address (sprint 21, 21.4a). Checked before anything is read: it says nothing about which emails hold an account.

bad_reset.meaning: POST /account/reset whose new passphrase breaks the account rule (field password: at least 12 characters) or whose confirm differs (field confirm) (sprint 21, 21.4a). Nothing written; the link stays live.
bad_reset.nextAction: Choose a passphrase of at least 12 characters and send the same one as confirm.

cross_site_verify.meaning: POST /account/verify flagged as arriving from a different site than this door (Sec-Fetch-Site, or Origin when that header is absent), the same guard as POST /login's cross_site_login (sprint 21, 21.4a). Refused before the body is read: nothing written.
cross_site_verify.nextAction: Verify from the link's own page (GET /account/verify/<token>); a script client sends neither header.

cross_site_resend.meaning: POST /account/resend flagged as arriving from a different site than this door, the same guard as POST /login's (sprint 21, 21.4a). Refused before the body is read: nothing sent.
cross_site_resend.nextAction: Ask from the door's own page (GET /account/resend).

cross_site_forgot.meaning: POST /account/forgot flagged as arriving from a different site than this door, the same guard as POST /login's (sprint 21, 21.4a). Refused before the body is read: nothing sent.
cross_site_forgot.nextAction: Ask from the door's own page (GET /account/forgot).

cross_site_reset.meaning: POST /account/reset flagged as arriving from a different site than this door, the same guard as POST /login's (sprint 21, 21.4a). Refused before the body is read: nothing written.
cross_site_reset.nextAction: Set the passphrase from the link's own page (GET /account/reset/<token>).

org_waiting.meaning: POST /orgs by an account whose own passphrase is right but whose email holds neither a used operator's code nor an approved request (sprint 21, 21.4a): a verified person still in line. The beta's orgs stay on the waitlist; nothing made but the proof's attempt.
org_waiting.nextAction: Wait for the approval (the person's status: GET /account; the operator's allow --request sends "You're in"), then create the org.

bad_org.meaning: POST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): a field is missing or malformed, checked before anything is read (`field`: email · password · name · slug · project · you, with a `note`): the slug (the org's address) takes a-z, 0-9 and single dashes, 2 to 40 characters, never opening or closing on a dash; the first project's slug 2 to 30 the same way. It says nothing about accounts or about which addresses orgs hold.
bad_org.nextAction: Fix the named field and send again.

org_name_reserved.meaning: POST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): the address (slug) is a name the platform uses: the first segment of one of the door's routes (GET /capabilities lists them) or one of its fixed words (src/orgnames.js). Checked before anything is read; nothing written.
org_name_reserved.nextAction: Choose another address for the org.

invalid_account.meaning: POST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): the email and the ACCOUNT passphrase do not prove an account. ONE answer for every case: no account for the email, an account with no passphrase yet, a wrong one, or a seat's own secret (a key an org's admin minted or set never creates an org). Nothing was written but the attempt, which counts in the account's lockout with the sign-in's failures.
invalid_account.nextAction: Use the passphrase you chose at sign-up (POST /signup with the operator's code); an account with none gets one there.

org_limit.meaning: POST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): this account has already created its org. During the beta an account creates ONE org (the free tier, docs/plan/PLATFORM.md §4 sprint 8), and may be a member of any number. Nothing written.
org_limit.nextAction: Use the org you created, or ask an org's admin to add you; a second org of your own is raised by hand on request.

org_name_taken.meaning: POST /orgs (sprint 7, 7.3): another org holds that address (asked only after the account is proven). Nothing written.
org_name_taken.nextAction: Choose another address for the org.

cross_site_org.meaning: POST /orgs was flagged as arriving from a different site than this door (Sec-Fetch-Site, or Origin when that header is absent), the same guard as POST /login's cross_site_login. Refused before the body is read: nothing written, not even an attempt.
cross_site_org.nextAction: Create the org from the door's own page (/orgs/new); a script client sends neither header and is never flagged.

org_unreachable.meaning: A call named an org (orgSlug, or ?orgSlug= on a brain:// resource) this connection does not act in: a seat's credential (a bearer key, a seat grant, a session) acts only in its own seat's org; an account grant only in the orgs its account holds an active seat in; and a JSON-RPC batch acts in one org (its FIRST call's: the current org when that call names none). An account grant whose own org no longer holds its seat names its org on every call: one that names none is refused, never acting in another org by default (sprint 7's review). The answer is the same whether the org named exists or not. Nothing was read or changed. `orgs` lists the orgs this connection may name.
org_unreachable.nextAction: Retry with one of the slugs in `orgs`, or leave orgSlug out to act in the current org; for a batch, send the call for another org on its own. To act in another org you belong to from a seat's connection, connect again by signing in with your account's passphrase.

already_seated.meaning: POST /orgs/seat accept (sprint 7's review, A1): your account already holds an active seat in that org (one account, one seat per org), so the waiting seat cannot become a second. HTTP 409; nothing changed.
already_seated.nextAction: Use the seat you hold there; ask that org's admin to withdraw the duplicate invitation.

choose_org.meaning: POST /login (JSON) with your ACCOUNT's passphrase (sprint 7's review, A1): your account holds seats in several orgs, or a seat of it waits for your yes (the owner's ruling, 2026-10-09), and the sign-in names none — the door never picks an org for you. HTTP 409; nothing was minted (the passphrase was right). `orgs` lists the orgs you hold an active seat in ({slug, name}); a waiting seat is answered on your org list (GET /orgs) after a browser sign-in.
choose_org.nextAction: Send the same sign-in with org: one of the slugs in `orgs` (or next naming a page of that org).

cross_site_seat.meaning: POST /orgs/seat was flagged as arriving from a different site than this door (Sec-Fetch-Site, or Origin when that header is absent), the front door's guard. Refused before the body is read: nothing changed.
cross_site_seat.nextAction: Answer the seat from your org list (GET /orgs) on the door's own page.

email_not_ascii.meaning: POST /signup (and Control's add-person) refused an email holding a letter outside plain ASCII (sprint 7's review, A5): an account's email has one spelling, and SQLite's lower() folds ASCII letters only. HTTP 422, refused before anything is read: nothing written.
email_not_ascii.nextAction: Use the ASCII spelling of the address.

shapes._doc: additive (sprint 3, B1; docs/plan/MCP.md §9 demand 2): the contribution shapes. ONE declaration, src/shapes.js SHAPES (a shape per lane of src/lanes.js), read by the filing doors, read, the contribution's page, the `formats` read and this contract (its fields, examples and places are GENERATED into `formats.shapes`). The fields new in B1 are each optional and checked at the door before anything is read or written: source, depends, open, next on every shape; audience, claim, channel, experiment on the gtm shape. src/transmission.js gateGrade never reads them: a missing one is never a refusal and the grade's reasons are unchanged.
shapes.refusal: 422 (the batch: that item's result) { error: 'bad_field', field (e.g. next.by, source[3].kind, depends[0]), hint, example, note } and nothing filed; the note points at formats {shape}
shapes.storage: migrate-047: contribution.shape (ONE JSON object of the new fields sent, NULL when none), next_by and next_who (next.by, next.who: real columns, idx_transmission_next_by (project, next_by) partial); a filing that sends none of the new fields writes the same INSERT as before
shapes.read: read and GET /contribution/:id answer the row with source, depends, open, next and the GTM four at the top level, each only when filed; the page (/contribution/:id?page=1) shows Next, Source (an artifact opens in the viewer, an http(s) link in a new tab), Still open, the GTM four in the Why region and Depends on in the refs region (a node opens on the Map, goal/<id> its goal, q/<qid> its question, a contribution its page, check/<id> stays a word)
shapes.nextWho: next.who is a person of the org by their id or email: only its FORM is checked, nothing is read, so the answer never says whether a person exists
shapes.happenedAt: sprint 3, the owner's MCQ 2026-10-01 (keep the filing time true, add the real date beside it): optional on every shape, when the work really happened: a date YYYY-MM-DD or a UTC date-time (ISO 8601, Z), never in the future (bad_field happenedAt), never before 2000-01-01. The row is still filed now (created_at, never backdated); migrate-051's contribution.happened_at keeps the date as sent and a date-time as toISOString(), returned by read and GET /contribution/:id as happened_at. Shown on the contribution's page (the trail: 'Happened <day> · filed <day>' when the days differ), on Build's rows (the time shown, 'filed <day>' in the title) and in a preview's line and text ('happened <day>'). The timelines a person reads use COALESCE(happened_at, created_at): Build's Newest (and the order inside Ranked and By goal), Home's goals moved this month, Broadcast's live picture's last 7 days and each dot's place; every count about the record (ids, rate limits, idempotency, the tallies, the queue, Home's metrics, Build's Moved this week) stays on created_at

A request that did not declare elicitation gets the check with confirm {asked: false, note}. The plain call (without fileOnConfirm) is unchanged. A read-only credential, a verb with no project, a client with no elicitation, a request that does not accept a stream or a batch gets the plain preview with confirm {asked: false, note}. The two calls (the verb, then the verb with confirm: true) are unchanged.
